deep_dive.title: All roads lead to Markov kernel networks: A representation theorem for discretization-stable learning
deep_dive.authors_text: S David Mis, Trevor Teolis, Ivan Dokmanić, Matti Lassas, Maarten V. de Hoop
deep_dive.abstract: Operator learning seeks to approximate function-to-function maps in a way that remains stable when the input discretization changes, a property sometimes called "discretization invariance". We consider a quantitative refinement of this idea, called $\textit{uniform discretization stability}$, which builds on a common representation of input functions and their discretizations as probability measures and provides a Hölder bound relating output changes to the Wasserstein distance between these measures. Our main result is a representation theorem showing all uniformly discretization stable operators can be written exactly as a $\textit{stable Markov kernel network}$---an abstract architecture that is a joint generalization of transformers, Fourier neural operators (FNO), Flowers, and other successful learned operators. Our representation theorem characterizes a design space for discretization-stable operator learning; designing new architectures becomes a question of which parts of a Markov kernel network to parameterize, and how. We further show that the read kernels of these networks can be realized as solutions of regularized variational problems, with particular choices of costs and regularizers recovering the kernels of transformers, FNO, Flowers, their hybrids, and beyond. This variational formulation provides a systematic approach to architecture design, together with sufficient conditions for uniform discretization stability.
deep_dive.tldr: The paper proves that all uniformly discretization-stable operators can be represented exactly as stable Markov kernel networks—a general architecture subsuming transformers, Fourier neural operators, and Flowers—and provides a variational framework for systematically designing such discretization-stable architectures.

detailed_reading.motivation: 算子学习需要逼近函数到函数的映射，并在输入离散化改变时保持稳定；仅有离散化细化下的收敛还不够，训练后的网络需要定量的稳定性保证。论文因此提出统一的概率测度视角，将连续输入函数与含噪离散样本都表示为图测度，并用关于 Wasserstein 距离的 Hölder 界刻画称为一致离散化稳定性的性质。其目标是回答哪些稳定性性质 relevant、哪些架构满足这些性质、以及如何系统刻画并探索这类架构的设计空间。
detailed_reading.method: 论文将紧度量空间上的函数 f 与其图测度 gamma_f 等同，将有限样本或含噪样本表示为 Dirac 混合测度 mu，并把算子学习视为从图测度到输出函数的映射；一致离散化稳定性要求输出变化受输入图测度间 Wasserstein 距离的 Hölder 界控制。核心建模对象是稳定 Markov 核网络，它交替使用由 Markov 核构成的非线性积分算子进行空间信息混合，以及逐点的通道混合算子进行嵌入空间信息混合。主定理通过构造性表示证明任一一致离散化稳定算子都可精确写成稳定 Markov 核网络；进一步将读出核刻画为正则化变分问题的解，通过选择代价函数与正则项获得 transformer、FNO、Flowers 及其混合架构的核，并给出保证一致离散化稳定性的充分条件。该工作以理论构造为主，不涉及端到端训练算法；推理时网络接收经验图测度并在任意空间点上输出函数值。
detailed_reading.result: 核心结果是表示定理：一致离散化稳定算子类与稳定 Markov 核网络类精确等价，而非近似等价；只要各组件满足相应稳定性，整个 Markov 核网络即具有一致离散化稳定性。变分刻画表明，特定代价与正则项可恢复 transformer 注意力、FNO、Flowers 及其混合形式的读出核，从而把新架构设计转化为选择 Markov 核网络中被参数化的部分以及参数化方式。论文还给出变分定义核的稳定性界和 Markov 核网络的通用逼近结果，提供了可复现的架构对应关系与充分条件，但未报告数值基准指标。
detailed_reading.conclusion: Markov 核网络为离散化稳定算子学习提供了自然且由表示定理固定的设计空间，使架构设计从经验拼装转为在统一抽象结构内选择参数化位置与变分正则化方式。该框架统一解释了 transformer、FNO、Flowers 等成功算子网络，并为自适应、混合及面向智能体的算子学习提供原则性设计语言。其理论价值在于把离散化与测量噪声误差纳入同一稳定性分析，并为系统探索新架构给出充分条件。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现细节包括将函数嵌入图空间上的 Radon 概率测度，使用 Wasserstein 距离与 Hölder 指数定义稳定性，并要求空间紧、输出集紧凸、基准测度支撑全空间等正则性条件。Markov 核网络的稳定化依赖空间混合核与通道混合算子的联合约束；变分读出核需要选择代价函数、正则项及相应参数，并通过充分条件验证稳定性。局限性在于表示定理是抽象存在性与精确表示，未直接给出有限样本训练、参数估计误差或计算复杂度的实用保证；变分问题可能仍需额外求解与近似，实际架构设计还需在表达能力、计算成本与稳定性条件之间权衡。

deep_dive.title: Efficient Learning of Differentiable MPC Policies on the GPU via Smoothed ADMM and First-Order Reinforcement Learning
deep_dive.authors_text: Jianghan Zhang, Roland Schwan, Gabriel Bravo-Palacios, John Zhang, Thomas Lew, Brian Plancher
deep_dive.abstract: Differentiable model predictive control (MPC) enables structured, constraint-aware policies to be optimized end-to-end. However, learning MPC policies faces two bottlenecks: (1) nonsmooth sensitivities at active-set transitions and (2) expensive policy evaluation, since each requires an optimization solve. We first introduce SmoothedTurboMPC, a GPU-parallel differentiable MPC solver combining sequential quadratic programming (SQP) with a log-barrier-smoothed alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) inner solver. Its design enables smooth gradients, exact sensitivities at convergence, and efficient execution on GPUs. Second, to efficiently train MPC policies, we pair our solver with first-order reinforcement learning (FORL) using Short-Horizon Actor-Critic (SHAC), which reuses rollout MPC solutions instead of repeatedly re-evaluating them. Comparisons with state of the art solvers show that the approach achieves up to $4.4\times$ higher end-to-end training throughput. On a vehicle racing task, our method achieves higher returns than MPC PPO with a $46\times$ speedup, training on 3.3 million transitions in only 7 minutes. Finally, we use the framework to train a more reliable MPC racing policy via RL with domain randomization, and validate it on a full-scale race car. We integrate our advances into the open-source TurboMPC solver.
deep_dive.tldr: The paper introduces **SmoothedTurboMPC**, a GPU-parallel differentiable MPC solver using log-barrier-smoothed ADMM within SQP, and pairs it with first-order RL (SHAC) that reuses rollout solutions to enable fast, stable end-to-end training of MPC policies, demonstrated with up to 4.4× higher training throughput and validated on a full-scale race car.

detailed_reading.motivation: 可微模型预测控制（MPC）能把约束感知的结构化策略端到端优化，但学习MPC策略面临两个瓶颈：约束主动集切换导致解映射敏感性不光滑，以及每次策略评估都需一次优化求解，训练昂贵。现有log-barrier内点法和反复重评估的RL-MPC方法未能同时高效解决这两个问题，因此需要协同设计GPU可微MPC求解器与一阶强化学习训练流程。
detailed_reading.method: 本文提出SmoothedTurboMPC：前向以SQP求解MPC非线性规划，内层在TurboMPC的ADMM中把投影式不等式更新替换为log-barrier近端更新，用扰动互补条件ν∘y=κ1平滑主动集边界，并在GPU上并行执行。反向传播对收敛KKT条件做隐式微分，通过伴随变量求外层次优问题的参数梯度，避免显式构造解对参数的雅可比；κ>0保证乘子与松弛不同时消失，κ→0时逼近原硬约束问题。训练端将求解器与Short-Horizon Actor-Critic（SHAC）一阶强化学习配对，复用rollout中的MPC解做单次策略更新而非在收集状态上反复重求解，并可结合域随机化学习MPC成本网络后部署MPC策略。
detailed_reading.result: 与最先进可微MPC求解器相比，该方案端到端训练吞吐最高提升4.4×；在车辆竞速仿真中，MPC-SHAC回报高于MPC PPO，墙钟时间加速46×，仅用7分钟训练3.3百万个transition。双积分器玩具实验中，log-barrier平滑使梯度下降从θ0=0.1和10两个初值均收敛到θ*=1.10并加速收敛；实车Lexus LC500水坑弯道测试中，学习策略完成全部四次试验、共12次过水坑，而名义MPC四次均打滑失控。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 结果表明，将GPU并行log-barrier平滑ADMM可微MPC与SHAC一阶强化学习结合，可在保持约束结构的同时显著提高MPC策略学习效率与梯度稳定性，并能在实车竞速场景获得比名义MPC更可靠的闭环表现。该工作把相关进展集成到开源TurboMPC中，为约束感知结构化策略的高效端到端学习提供了可复现路径，但平滑参数带来的近似偏差和每步优化求解成本仍需权衡。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现包括SQP外层加log-barrier平滑ADMM内层、以近端更新替代投影、通过KKT雅可比和伴随变量做隐式微分，以及SHAC短视界actor-critic的单次一阶更新复用rollout解；双积分器实验取H=6、学习率η=0.1、初值θ0∈{0.1,10}，竞速实验统计3.3M transitions与7分钟训练时间。方法以κ控制平滑度与原NLP近似误差，κ过小仍可能不光滑、过大引入偏差；每次策略评估仍需MPC求解，实车验证依赖域随机化且平台和任务范围有限，结论外推需谨慎。

deep_dive.title: Projected Neural Additive Models as Universal Approximators
deep_dive.authors_text: Nhon N. Phan, Qiang Du, John D. Clayton, WaiChing Sun
deep_dive.abstract: Neural additive models (NAMs) offer interpretability but lack expressivity due to their rigid additive structure, whereas multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) achieve universal approximation at the cost of transparency. We establish the first theoretical foundation for projected neural additive models (PNAMs), which augment NAMs with a learnable linear transformation $\boldsymbol{T}$ to capture cross-variable interactions. While standard NAMs cannot approximate even the simplest interaction term $χ_1 χ_2$ because their cross-derivatives are identically zero, we prove that PNAMs are universal approximators and characterize the minimum number of projections required for exact polynomial representation. Furthermore, we derive an approximation rate of $\mathcal{O}(M^{-s / (N - 1)})$ for $\mathcal{C}^s$ functions (i.e., functions with $s$ continuous derivatives), where $M$ denotes the number of projections and $N$ the input dimension; this rate is known to be optimal for ridge function approximation. To recover interpretability from the projected inputs, we introduce structured sparsity regularizers and post-hoc symbolic regression techniques that enable global input ranking, parameter pruning, and the conversion of learned bases into compact analytical expressions. Experiments on knot theory invariants, MNIST, and phase field fracture mechanics demonstrate that PNAMs match or surpass similar architectures in accuracy while discovering salient features and yielding symbolic models with orders of magnitude fewer parameters.
deep_dive.tldr: Projected neural additive models (PNAMs), which add a learnable linear projection to neural additive models to capture cross-variable interactions, are proven to be universal approximators with an optimal ridge-function approximation rate while retaining interpretability through structured sparsity and symbolic regression.

detailed_reading.motivation: 神经加性模型（NAM）以单变量形状函数提供可解释性，但其刚性加性结构导致交叉导数恒为零，甚至无法表示最简单的交互项χ1χ2；多层感知机虽具有通用逼近能力却缺乏透明性。本文旨在为带可学习线性投影的PNAM建立首个理论基础，并在保持表达力的同时恢复可解释性。
detailed_reading.method: 给定监督数据{(χ,y)}，PNAM将输入经可学习矩阵T投影为z=Tχ，再以加权和Σζ_i f_i(z_i)输出，其中f_i由独立一维MLP或多项式基参数化，并可选用固定高斯傅里叶特征增强高频表达能力；训练时联合优化T、权重ζ和MLP参数，并引入结构化稀疏正则以进行全局输入排序、交互筛选和剪枝。理论部分先用Stone–Weierstrass定理将连续函数逼近转化为多项式表示，再证明PNAM可通过岭函数叠加精确复现多变量多项式，从而得到通用逼近性，并借助Jackson定理推导逼近率；推理阶段还可对学习到的一维基做事后符号回归，将基函数转化为紧凑解析表达式。
detailed_reading.result: 论文证明标准NAM因交叉导数为零而不能逼近χ1χ2，而PNAM是通用逼近器，并给出精确表示任意N变量P次多项式所需最小投影数的构造性上界与参数计数下界。对C^s函数，PNAM达到O(M^{-s/(N−1)})的逼近率，其中M为投影数、N为输入维数，该速率是岭函数逼近的已知最优速率。在纽结理论不变量、MNIST和相场断裂力学实验中，PNAM在精度上匹配或超过同类架构，同时识别显著特征，并得到参数量少数量级的符号模型。
detailed_reading.conclusion: PNAM通过单个可学习线性投影加一维非线性基，弥补了NAM缺乏交互表达能力的理论缺陷，并在通用逼近性与最优岭函数逼近率之间建立了联系。结构化稀疏与事后符号回归使其能够进行全局输入排序、参数剪枝和紧凑表达式提取，因此适合交互阶数较高、沿少数方向稠密或先验未知的问题。其加性基结构仍不适合紧凑表示除法等操作，精确物理定律恢复应留给专门的符号回归方法。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键理论点包括NAM的交叉导数恒为零、PNAM用投影方向捕获跨变量耦合、以及多项式精确表示所需最小M的上界与下界；逼近率中的常数依赖紧域、光滑阶s、维数N和函数范数界B。实现上，每个投影对应一个一维MLP基，可选傅里叶特征由固定高斯分布N(0,σ²)采样且初始化后不训练，T和ζ可优化以产生更稀疏解，结构化稀疏正则用于全局排序和剪枝。复杂度与约束在于M通常远小于成对交互数N(N−1)/2，但复杂交互可能需要很大M；局限性是加性结构难以紧凑逼近除法等非加性操作，符号回归主要用于剪枝而非保证恢复精确物理定律。

deep_dive.title: Preference-Augmented Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Sensitive Navigation
deep_dive.authors_text: Zhaofan Zhang, Yue Chang, Rufeng Chen, Hechang Chen, Sihong Xie, Hui Xiong
deep_dive.abstract: Ensuring safe and reliable navigation under diverse sources of uncertainty remains a central challenge for autonomous systems. Within distributional reinforcement learning (DistRL), Implicit Quantile Networks (IQN) have attracted interest for navigation under uncertainty because they enable risk adaptation through flexible quantile sampling. Existing approaches, however, typically use a fixed or randomly sampled Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) level during training and adjust the risk level during deployment using hand-tuned hyperparameters or external sensor signals. This scalar-CVaR formulation confines learning to a narrow family of tail-risk preferences, creating a mismatch between training-time preference exposure and deployment-time risk adjustment. We instead represent variations in risk preference as shifts in quantile-weight distributions and expose the agent to diverse preferences through preference-guided exploration. At deployment, we optimize against the worst-case preference distribution to derive a conservative policy that accounts for multiple risk profiles. This reduces hyperparameter tuning and reliance on limited sensor signals under partial observability. Experiments across simulated environments and vehicle platforms show that our method reduces collisions while improving task success.
deep_dive.tldr: The paper proposes PAIQN, a preference-augmented distributional reinforcement learning method that represents risk preferences as quantile-weight distributions, trains with diverse preference-guided exploration, and deploys a distributionally robust conservative policy to improve risk-sensitive navigation by reducing collisions and increasing task success.

detailed_reading.motivation: 现有基于分布强化学习与IQN的风险敏感导航方法通常在训练时使用固定或随机采样的标量CVaR水平，并在部署时依靠手工超参数或外部传感器信号调整风险水平，导致训练期偏好暴露与部署期风险适应不匹配。标量CVaR还把学习限制在狭窄的尾部风险偏好族内，难以在部分可观测和潜在环境不确定性下可靠推断合适的保守程度。
detailed_reading.method: 本文将风险偏好表示为分位数权重分布而非单一CVaR参数：训练时从Dirichlet分布采样权重，并通过随全局交互步退火的偏差项构造非均匀分位数权重，将其用于偏好贪婪动作选择，并与epsilon随机探索结合；在构造Bellman目标时也独立采样偏好权重以选择目标动作，但目标回报分位数与IQN分位Huber损失保持不变。部署时将分位数权重分布视为不确定量，在偏好分布模糊集上做分布鲁棒优化，以最坏偏好分布评估动作并得到保守策略。
detailed_reading.result: 在多个模拟导航环境和不同车辆平台上的实验表明，PAIQN相较IQN在含障碍与阴影涡流等不确定场景中降低碰撞率并提高任务成功率，且在多数评估风险偏好设置下能够成功导航。理论分析给出偏好加权引入的Bellman误差上界随退火参数趋于零而消失，说明训练期偏好扰动不会造成持续的方向性偏差。
detailed_reading.conclusion: PAIQN通过分位数权重分布统一了训练期的多样风险偏好暴露与部署期的鲁棒保守决策，减少了对固定CVaR映射和有限传感器信号的依赖，从而提升部分可观测环境下风险敏感导航的安全性与任务成功率。
detailed_reading.key_details: 实现上使用K个固定中点分位数，Dirichlet浓度b控制偏好形状，退火偏差采用Delta_t=Delta_0 max(t,1)^-(1+eta)，epsilon按线性调度退火；偏好权重在同一状态的所有候选动作间共享，目标动作使用独立采样的偏好权重但不对目标回报重新加权。理论界为||Q_{t+1}-Q*||<=gamma||Q_t-Q*||+gamma D/K+2gamma D Delta_t，其中D=(r_max-r_min)/(1-gamma)，需Delta_t<=1且依赖理想化同步Bellman更新等假设；实验细节与真实部署限制在可见文本中未完全展开。

deep_dive.title: Capturability-Aware Footstep Planning in Cluttered Environments: A Recursively Feasible Sequential MPC on Axis-Aligned Safe Corridors
deep_dive.authors_text: Athanasios Kyriakopoulos, Shubham S. Kumbhar, Kunal S. Narkhede, Abhijeet M. Kulkarni, Ioannis Poulakakis
deep_dive.abstract: A fundamental aspect of humanoid footstep planning is to jointly guarantee obstacle avoidance and locomotion stability. This paper presents a capturability-aware sequential Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for Linear Inverted Pendulum (LIP)-based humanoid footstep planning in the presence of obstacles. The proposed method combines obstacle avoidance with capturability constraints through safe corridors constructed as sequences of intersecting rectangles, yielding a sequential MPC framework with recursive feasibility guarantees for the LIP-based planning layer. The planner autonomously adapts to constrained scenarios, switching to in-place walking when obstructions---such as doors assumed to be open during planning but unexpectedly found to be closed during execution---block forward motion. Performance is largely independent of the prediction horizon, allowing high success rates while keeping the computational cost low. The approach is validated in high-fidelity simulations with the humanoid robot Digit, demonstrating a practical solution for capturable humanoid footstep planning in cluttered environments.
deep_dive.tldr: This paper proposes a capturability-aware sequential MPC framework for LIP-based humanoid footstep planning that uses axis-aligned safe corridors to jointly ensure obstacle avoidance and locomotion stability with recursive feasibility, enabling autonomous in-place walking when forward motion is blocked and validating the approach on the humanoid robot Digit.

detailed_reading.motivation: 人形机器人在杂乱、以人为中心的环境中导航时，足步规划必须同时保证避障与运动稳定性，但现有基于降阶模型的方法往往只生成无碰撞路径而缺乏显式可捕获性保证，而强调步态稳定的方法又常忽略障碍约束。本文针对这一空白，研究在障碍环境中具有递归可行性的可捕获性感知足步规划。
detailed_reading.method: 方法以线性倒立摆（LIP）为规划模型，将状态分解为发散运动分量（DCM）与收敛运动分量（CCM），并采用步到步动力学、足端可达集和N步捕获区域约束；将自由空间表示为轴对齐安全走廊（AASC），即一串相交矩形，并在每个矩形内构造内接的可行足步区域，使足步限制在该区域内时同时保证COM不越界和N步可捕获。随后沿走廊构建顺序MPC：每个局部MPC只优化当前矩形内的足步，并通过捕获区域/终端约束与矩形间切换策略保持递归可行性；当检测到前进受阻（例如规划时假定打开但执行时关闭的门）时，规划器自动减速并切换为原地踏步。
detailed_reading.result: 在高保真MuJoCo仿真中以Digit人形机器人验证，并在随机生成的轴对齐矩形障碍环境中与Narkhede2022方法比较；结果表明该方法能在保持高成功率的同时显著降低对预测时域的依赖，计算成本较低。关键发现是显式可捕获性约束带来内在安全性和优雅降级：当前进路径被意外阻塞时，机器人会自主减速并原地踏步，而仅依赖纯几何安全走廊的方法难以提供这种保证。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 本文提出了一种将避障与可捕获性统一到顺序MPC中的足步规划框架，通过轴对齐安全走廊及其内接可捕获足步区域，为基于LIP的人形机器人规划层提供递归可行性保证。该方法在杂乱环境中兼顾无碰撞导航与可捕获步态，并在受阻场景中表现出安全退化能力，为实际人形机器人足步规划提供了有前景的解决方案。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现包括：以LIP常高COM模型和DCM/CCM分解建立离散步态动力学，使用步长T、固有频率ωo=√(g/H)、足端可达边界以及递归计算的N步捕获区域；安全走廊由可分离的轴对齐矩形组成，便于高效碰撞检测和盒约束，每个矩形内再求内接足步区域，并依据DCM偏移位于捕获区域、CCM偏移有界来保证约束一致性；顺序MPC沿走廊局部求解，配合矩形切换条件和捕获区域终端约束保证递归可行性，因而计算复杂度较低且性能对预测时域不敏感。局限包括依赖轴对齐矩形障碍近似、采用降阶LIP模型、主要在MuJoCo仿真中验证，以及走廊构造与切换策略对复杂非矩形环境的适用性仍需进一步检验。

deep_dive.title: Beyond Semantic Classes: Online Physical Parameter Estimation via Embedding-Conditioned Gaussian Mixtures
deep_dive.authors_text: Alexander Borca-Tasciuc, Prayag Sharma, Franck Djeumou
deep_dive.abstract: Enabling robots to infer interaction-relevant physical properties from vision before contact would improve planning and control in unstructured environments. Vision provides useful pre-contact information, but appearance alone is often ambiguous: visually similar regions can induce different friction, stiffness, or sinkage responses upon contact. Existing approaches often collapse this ambiguity to a point estimate or aggregate experience through fixed semantic classes, limiting their ability to preserve distinct physical regimes. Instead, we propose a real-time estimator that replaces semantic class indexing with an interaction-grounded Gaussian-mixture posterior over latent physical parameters, conditioned directly on continuous visual embeddings. Our approach maintains interaction-derived Gaussian parameter estimates, typically from inverse modeling, as mixture components while using embedding similarity to retrieve and weight relevant past interactions for each new query region. A support-aware fusion mechanism incorporates a conditional generative prior model when interaction history is sparse, while a learned embedding refinement improves retrieval relevance without discretizing the representation. Our experiments show that the estimator recovers multimodal physical beliefs, rejects unrelated interaction history, avoids spatial map discretization, and evaluates at controller rates. In a high-fidelity autonomous racing simulation with unknown low- and high-friction surface regions, the posterior enables the controller to adapt over repeated laps as interaction evidence accumulates, improving performance while maintaining friction-aware behavior.
deep_dive.tldr: The paper proposes a real-time, interaction-grounded Gaussian-mixture posterior over latent physical parameters conditioned directly on continuous visual embeddings, avoiding semantic-class discretization and enabling robots to retain multimodal physical beliefs from sparse contact experience for improved planning and control.

detailed_reading.motivation: 视觉可在接触前提供摩擦、刚度、沉陷等物理参数线索，但外观与物理响应之间存在多义性，相似视觉区域可能对应不同物理状态。现有方法常把这种歧义压缩为点估计，或用固定语义类聚合经验，导致类内不同物理状态被平均且词汇外材料污染类级信念，因此需要保留多峰分布并可由交互证据实时更新的估计器。
detailed_reading.method: 方法将每次短轨迹交互通过逆建模得到局部物理参数的高斯信念 φ_i=(μ_i,Σ_i)，并与对应区域视觉嵌入 e_i 一起存入历史 D_N；查询区域用冻结视觉编码器得到嵌入，经学习到的残差细化 e=unit(bar e+α r_η(bar e)) 后用归一化指数余弦核 K_h 计算历史权重 w_i，形成显式高斯混合历史后验 sum w_i N(μ_i,Σ_i)。为处理历史稀疏，计算未归一化核质量 M 和置信度 ρ=M/(M+κ)，将历史后验与条件生成先验按 ρ 融合；先验可直接作用于 z，也可作用于高斯信念参数 φ 并通过扩散模型采样 S 个 (μ,Σ) 分量，使最终后验仍是可解析评估和采样的高斯混合。嵌入细化用 HDBSCAN 对无标签图像嵌入聚类得到原型方向，训练轻量残差网络使聚类样本靠近原型、噪声样本保持原嵌入，损失含聚类目标、非噪声幅值正则和噪声幅值惩罚，推理时仅改变检索几何不离散化表示。系统在 BeamNG 前视相机数据上以 DINOv3 嵌入和 FIFO 缓冲、接触点投影关联局部 Normal-Inverse-Gamma 估计，并在自动驾驶赛车闭环控制中按控制器频率查询后验。
detailed_reading.result: 实验表明该估计器能恢复多峰物理信念，拒绝不相关交互历史，避免空间地图离散化，并在交互数据库增长时以控制器频率完成查询。语义瓶颈实验显示其避免类平均和词汇外污染，且核可组合空间邻近等非视觉相似性。在高保真自动驾驶赛车仿真中，面对未知低摩擦和高摩擦区域，后验随重复圈次积累交互证据使控制器逐步适应，提升性能并保持摩擦感知行为。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 论文提出以连续视觉嵌入为条件、以交互导出的高斯信念为分量的在线物理参数估计框架，用支持感知融合和检索空间细化在无语义类索引下保留多模态后验。该后验可直接供模型预测控制等下游模块评估和采样，在未知摩擦区域闭环赛车任务中展示了随交互证据累积的适应能力。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现包括 DINOv3 冻结嵌入、FIFO 图像与位姿缓冲、接触点投影到最近有效帧、Normal-Inverse-Gamma 局部参数估计、指数余弦核带宽 h、支持系数 κ、先验采样数 S 和细化强度 α；残差细化损失含 λ_cluster 与 λ_noise 正则，HDBSCAN 原型仅用于训练检索嵌入而非作为地形类。先验可用条件扩散模型在高斯信念空间生成分量，从而保持显式混合并便于 GPU 采样；计算复杂度随历史交互数 N 和先验样本数 S 线性增长，需依赖检索或缓冲管理满足实时性。方法假设每次交互可由逆建模给出高斯局部信念，且后验质量依赖嵌入空间中物理相关相似性的几何；HDBSCAN 聚类与原型可能受无标签数据分布和超参影响。实验主要为 BeamNG 仿真与有限真实车辆轨迹评估，跨平台大规模定量指标和更多真实环境验证仍是局限。

deep_dive.title: A Hierarchical Variational Inequality Approach to Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking with Nonlinear Shared Constraints
deep_dive.authors_text: Tatiana Tatarenko, Puya Latafat, Alberto Bemporad
deep_dive.abstract: We study the computation of variational generalized Nash equilibria (v-GNE) in games with strongly monotone pseudo-gradients and nonlinear convex shared constraints. We show that the v-GNE problem is exactly equivalent to a hierarchical variational inequality, whose lower level is given by the gradient of a smooth convex penalty of the constraint violation over the local action sets. Building on this reformulation, we propose a hierarchical regularization scheme that operates entirely in the primal space and requires only projections onto the local action sets. In the centralized setting, we prove last-iterate squared distance convergence to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t^{\scriptscriptstyle 2/3})$ under a local error bound condition, which holds, e.g., under Slater's condition, improved to $O(1/t)$ under a global error bound condition. We then extend the scheme to the partial-decision information setting, where the agents communicate over a network and maintain local estimates of the joint action. We derive a distributed algorithm with a constant stepsize operating in the primal space and converging to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t)$.
deep_dive.tldr: The paper reformulates variational generalized Nash equilibrium seeking under nonlinear shared constraints as a hierarchical variational inequality with a penalty-based lower level, enabling primal-space centralized and distributed projection algorithms with last-iterate convergence guarantees.

detailed_reading.motivation: 广义纳什均衡问题中，智能体既通过代价函数耦合，也通过共享约束耦合；实际系统如电力网络、充电协调和交通网络常具有非线性共享约束，且智能体只能获得局部信息。现有基于KKT条件的原始-对偶方法需要维护和协调对偶变量，并在非线性约束下失去全局Lipschitz性、常步长保证或需集中式线搜索，因此需要一种完全在原始空间、仅依赖局部动作集投影的均衡求解方法。
detailed_reading.method: 论文针对强单调伪梯度和非线性凸共享约束的博弈，证明v-GNE问题等价于一个分层变分不等式：上层为博弈伪梯度，下层为约束违反的某个光滑凸罚函数梯度在局部动作集上的变分不等式。基于此提出集中式分层正则化格式，每步仅对局部动作集做投影，不引入对偶变量；随后扩展到部分决策信息场景，智能体在连通无向图上通信并维护联合动作的局部估计，采用常步长的分布式原始空间算法，通过局部估计一致性与投影更新逼近v-GNE。
detailed_reading.result: 在集中式设置下，作者证明末迭代平方距离收敛到v-GNE：局部误差界条件（例如Slater条件成立时）下速率为O(1/t^{2/3})，全局误差界条件（例如线性共享约束与多面体局部集）下提升为O(1/t)。在部分决策信息设置下，分布式常步长算法在局部误差界条件和有界动作集下以O(1/t)速率收敛到v-GNE；实验在随机非线性网络约束和多智能体线性共享约束问题上验证性能，并与基于KKT的提升原始-对偶方法进行比较。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 该工作给出了v-GNE的精确分层变分不等式重构，说明无需对偶变量或耦合可行集投影即可在原始空间求解非线性共享约束下的广义纳什均衡。所提集中式与分布式算法分别具有可证明的末迭代收敛速率，分布式版本避免对偶变量通信并降低计算与通信负担，为局部信息下的GNE寻求提供了新框架。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键假设包括博弈为凸博弈、伪梯度强单调、共享约束函数凸且连续可微、局部动作集投影易计算；集中式分析依赖局部或全局误差界条件，分布式分析还要求连通无向图和有界动作集。方法的核心是先验结构是把耦合可行集刻画为光滑凸罚函数的最小点集，从而下层VI对应凸优化并支持末迭代分析；算法仅使用局部动作集投影和常步长，不需要对偶变量共识或集中式线搜索。局限在于收敛速率依赖误差界/Slater类条件，分布式结果需有界动作集，且集中式方案仍需全局算子信息，实验主要覆盖随机实例和线性共享约束对比。

deep_dive.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach
deep_dive.authors_text: Zhen Qin, Zhiyao Zhang, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu
deep_dive.abstract: Stochastic bilevel optimization provides a general framework for many machine learning applications, such as hyperparameter learning, data reweighting, language model alignment, and actor-critic reinforcement learning. However, most existing bilevel optimization methods treat matrix-valued gradients as flattened vectors and perform optimization in the resulting vectorized space, ignoring the matrix structures common in modern neural networks. Moreover, the lower-level (LL) problem curvature can induce significant spectral imbalance in the upper-level (UL) geometry. Such limitations of existing bilevel optimization methods motivate us to develop BiMuon, a geometry-aware stochastic bilevel optimization method that integrates implicit hypergradient estimation in bilevel optimization with Muon-style orthogonalized updates at the UL. To our knowledge, BiMuon is the first stochastic BLO method with Muon-style orthogonalized matrix updates and an $O(ε^{-4})$ iteration-complexity guarantee, matching the best-known rates achieved by Muon-type methods based on matrix parameterizations. To improve computational and parallel efficiency for models with multiple matrix parameters, we further study BiMuon for blockwise diagonal matrix approximation and derive a relative stepsize allocation rule based on UL progress and blockwise LL sensitivity. We evaluate BiMuon on representation learning and blockwise bilevel optimization, providing empirical support for our methods.
deep_dive.tldr: BiMuon is a geometry-aware stochastic bilevel optimization method that integrates implicit hypergradient estimation with Muon-style orthogonalized matrix updates, achieves an \(O(\epsilon^{-4})\) iteration-complexity guarantee, and extends to blockwise diagonal approximation with sensitivity-based stepsize allocation.

detailed_reading.motivation: 现有随机双层优化方法多将矩阵梯度展平为向量并在向量化空间更新，忽略了神经网络参数的矩阵结构；同时下层问题的曲率会通过双层复合放大上层几何中的谱不平衡，使超梯度被少数奇异方向主导。为此，作者提出几何感知的随机双层优化方法BiMuon，将隐式超梯度估计与Muon式正交化矩阵更新结合。
detailed_reading.method: BiMuon先用热启动随机梯度下降跟踪下层解，再用截断Neumann级数近似下层Hessian逆并估计上层超梯度，最后在上层参数更新处对超梯度或动量矩阵施加Muon式极分解正交化；精确极分解可用SVD实现，实际采用有限步Newton-Schulz迭代近似。针对多矩阵参数模型，作者进一步研究块对角矩阵近似，并依据上层优化进展与各块下层敏感性分配相对步长。理论分析覆盖精确极分解和有限Newton-Schulz两种版本，并在表示学习和块双层优化任务上评估。
detailed_reading.result: 作者用二次双层案例证明下层Hessian条件数会在上层Hessian中被平方放大，即κ(H_UL)=κ(H_LL)^2，且超梯度奇异幅度按x_i/h_i^2缩放，说明下层曲率各向异性会直接造成上层超梯度的谱不平衡。理论上，BiMuon的精确极分解版与有限Newton-Schulz版均达到E||∇Φ(X_R)||_*=O(T^{-1/4})的有限时间收敛率，对应Õ(ε^{-4})样本复杂度，与随机单层Muon型方法已知最优结果匹配。实验在表示学习和块双层优化上提供了经验支持。
detailed_reading.conclusion: BiMuon是首个采用Muon式正交化矩阵更新并具有O(ε^{-4})迭代复杂度保证的随机双层优化方法，表明将双层超梯度估计与上层正交化更新解耦可在保留标准随机双层估计流程的同时利用矩阵谱几何。块对角近似与基于上层进展和下层敏感性的步长分配可提升多矩阵参数模型的计算与并行效率。
detailed_reading.key_details: 问题设定为上层非凸、下层μ强凸的随机双层优化，超梯度由隐函数定理给出，并用H^{-1}≈ηΣ_{i=0}^Q(I-ηH)^i的截断Neumann级数通过Hessian-向量积估计；下层用热启动SGD跟踪，上层以极分解或有限Newton-Schulz近似得到正交化更新。关键误差来源包括下层跟踪误差、Neumann截断误差以及有限Newton-Schulz近似误差，理论同时处理精确极分解与有限NS版本；块对角近似引入块间耦合忽略误差，并用上层进展和块级下层敏感性确定相对步长。复杂度为Õ(ε^{-4})，与单层Muon型方法最优已知率一致；实验范围限于表示学习与块双层优化，完整实证对比需参考正文。

deep_dive.title: Selected-Risk Calibration for Feasibility at Returned Decisions
deep_dive.authors_text: Raghav Thind, Youran Sun, Ling Liang, Haizhao Yang
deep_dive.abstract: When an optimization problem uses a surrogate constraint, a decision that is feasible for the surrogate need not be feasible for the true constraint. We propose Selected-Risk Calibration (SRC), a framework that calibrates a learned constraint against the optimizer's returned decisions for objectives drawn from a given distribution. SRC guarantees that, with probability at least $1-δ$, every margin it certifies on held-out objectives has selected risk, the probability that the returned decision is infeasible, of at most $γ$. We also show that the random-input coverage guarantee of split conformal prediction does not bound the selected risk, and that likelihood-ratio reweighting for feedback covariate shift does not apply when the learned constraint is active at the returned decision. Our experiments show that a conformal margin covering about $90\%$ of random inputs covered as few as $17\%$ of the returned decisions, and every certified margin had a violation rate below its target on unseen objectives. Moreover, at equal cost, SRC's correction had fewer or equal infeasible solutions to the baselines in 57 of 62 comparisons. The SRC framework applies to any setting in which a surrogate model chooses a decision whose feasibility can be verified for a sample of instances.
deep_dive.tldr: The paper proposes Selected-Risk Calibration (SRC), a finite-sample, distribution-free framework that calibrates a learned surrogate constraint against the optimizer’s returned decisions to guarantee that, with high probability, the probability a returned decision violates the true constraint is bounded—addressing the failure of standard conformal random-input coverage to ensure feasibility at selected decisions.

detailed_reading.motivation: 在约束学习优化中，代理模型约束可行并不代表真实约束可行；优化器会返回在代理可行域边界附近、由目标函数驱动的决策点，而 split conformal 只保证随机输入点的覆盖率，不能约束该返回决策的真实不可行概率。论文因此提出以优化器返回决策为校准对象，直接控制 selected risk，即随机目标下返回决策违反真实约束的概率。
detailed_reading.method: 方法以已训练代理约束 hhat、随机校准样本得到的 conformal 边距 qhat 和可加连续修正 g 为基础，部署可行域为 {x: hhat(x)+qhat+g(x)≤0}；对从目标分布 Q 独立抽取的目标 c 求解 min c(x) 得到返回决策 x*(c)，再用真实约束 oracle 检查 h(x*(c))>0 形成伯努利不可行指标。SRC 对候选边距或修正 g 在这些返回决策上估计 selected risk，并用有限样本置信上界进行认证：仅当上界不超过目标 γ 时认证该边距，多个候选时用联合界控制总体置信度 1-δ；部署时选择已认证的修正或边距，优化流程无需改变化。
detailed_reading.result: 理论上证明随机输入 conformal 覆盖本身不能界定 selected risk，且当学习约束在返回决策处 active、残差连续时，返回决策分布与校准数据分布对几乎每个校准样本互奇异，因此 feedback covariate shift 的似然比重加权不适用。实验显示覆盖约 90% 随机输入的 conformal 边距在返回决策上覆盖率可低至 17%；所有被 SRC 认证的边距在未见目标上的违约率均低于目标，并且在等成本下 SRC 修正相对基线在 62 次比较中有 57 次不可行解更少或持平。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 论文表明，OCL 中代理约束的随机点覆盖保证不能直接转化为优化器返回决策的真实可行性保证，必须针对 solver 返回的决策进行校准。SRC 提供了有限样本、分布无关的 selected-risk 控制框架，可后接于常规训练的代理模型，并适用于任何由代理模型选择决策且可离线核验样本可行性的场景。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键设置包括真实约束 h 只能通过昂贵 oracle 或模拟器离线查询，代理 hhat 用约束数据训练，conformal 校准样本大小为 m、水平为 α，目标从 Q 抽取且给定建模范式后独立于其他随机性，目标风险阈值 γ、置信水平 δ 和可选容差 τ 为超参；SRC 的复杂度主要来自对每个候选修正/边距在 n 个抽样目标上重复求解优化并查询 oracle，若候选多需多重检验或联合界。理论依赖可测选择、有限样本 Bernoulli 风险上界和固定目标分布 Q，实验为三个仿真基准；局限是需可离线核验返回决策、候选修正族和样本量影响认证与计算成本，且理论使用精确最小化器而认证适用于实际 solver 返回解。

deep_dive.title: BATCH: Behavior Alignment for Cross-Embodiment Learning from Humans
deep_dive.abstract: Human demonstrations provide a scalable source of diverse manipulation data, but leveraging them for robot learning remains challenging due to differences in embodiment, viewpoint, action spaces, and temporal structure. We introduce BATCH, a cross-embodiment learning framework that explicitly aligns human and robot behaviors. BATCH learns self-supervised temporal representations with a cycle-consistency objective to establish cross-embodiment correspondences without manual annotation. We further introduce two complementary training objectives that leverage these correspondences within an autoregressive videoaction diffusion model: behavior-aligned co-training and human-to-robot style transfer. On real-world manipulation tasks, BATCH improves generalization to unseen task configurations compared with training on unaligned data and prior cross-embodiment baselines, with additional gains from the style-transfer objective. Our results demonstrate that explicit behavior alignment enables more effective transfer from human demonstrations to robot policies.
deep_dive.tldr: BATCH is a cross-embodiment learning framework that explicitly aligns human and robot behaviors via self-supervised cycle-consistent temporal representations and behavior-aligned co-training/style transfer, enabling more effective transfer from human demonstrations to robot manipulation policies and improved generalization.

detailed_reading.motivation: 人类演示数据可扩展且任务多样，但直接用于机器人学习会受具身形态、视角、动作空间和时间结构差异的限制。论文旨在通过显式对齐人类与机器人行为，提升从人类演示到机器人策略的迁移效率与泛化能力。
detailed_reading.method: BATCH 先利用带循环一致性目标的自监督时序表征学习，在无需人工标注的情况下建立跨具身对应关系。随后在自回归视频-动作扩散模型中引入两个互补训练目标：行为对齐协同训练和人类到机器人风格迁移，使对齐后的跨具身数据共同参与策略学习。整体流程以人类演示与机器人数据为输入，先学习时序对应，再通过扩散模型进行动作生成训练与推理。
detailed_reading.result: 在真实世界操作任务上，BATCH 相比使用未对齐数据训练以及先前跨具身基线，在未见任务配置上的泛化表现更好。加入风格迁移目标还能带来额外性能提升，说明显式行为对齐有助于更有效地利用人类演示。
detailed_reading.conclusion: 结果表明，跨具身学习的关键在于显式对齐人类与机器人行为；通过自监督对应关系与协同训练/风格迁移结合，可以更有效地将人类演示迁移为机器人策略，并改善对新任务配置的泛化。
detailed_reading.key_details: 关键实现包括自监督时序表征、循环一致性对应学习、无人工标注的跨具身匹配，以及在自回归视频-动作扩散模型中使用行为对齐协同训练和人类到机器人风格迁移两个目标。评估基于真实世界操作任务，并与未对齐数据和先前跨具身基线比较；摘要未给出具体网络规模、超参数、数据规模和计算复杂度，对应关系质量及人类与机器人域差异可能是主要约束。

quick_skim.title: A Unified Inertial Encoder for Human and Humanoid Motion
quick_skim.authors_text: Yutian Chen, Shibo Zhao, Rocky Duan, Karen Liu, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi, Yuheng Qiu, Koushil Sreenath
quick_skim.abstract: Learning humanoid state estimation and language-grounded motion understanding from robot recordings ties training coverage to the robot's motion repertoire. Human motion datasets offer broader coverage, yet transferring this knowledge requires overcoming differences in body geometry, sensing, and physical disturbances. To enable this transfer, we propose a unified inertial encoder whose shared inertial interface uses kinematic IMU synthesis to represent human and humanoid motion at corresponding body sites. Within this common input space, joint training on human and kinematically retargeted humanoid motion combines velocity estimation and motion--text alignment with continuous-time encoding and sensor and motion randomization. The resulting model transfers zero-shot to a physical Unitree G1 without physics simulation, real-robot training trajectories, or fine-tuning, achieving the lowest velocity error among evaluated methods across five datasets, including 0.099m/s on real G1. Its motion-description retrieval also extends to retargeted G1 motion categories observed only in human training, demonstrating how human motion knowledge can support the generalization of humanoid inertial odometry and language-grounded motion understanding.
quick_skim.tldr: The paper proposes a unified inertial encoder trained on human and kinematically retargeted humanoid motion through a shared inertial interface, enabling zero-shot transfer to a physical Unitree G1 for accurate inertial odometry and language-grounded motion understanding without simulation, real-robot trajectories, or fine-tuning.

quick_skim.title: Open-Source Multi-Fidelity EMT Modeling of Data Center Loads for Power System Studies
quick_skim.authors_text: Xingyu Zhao, Yingyi Tang, Junbo Zhao
quick_skim.abstract: Characterizing data center-grid interactions under rapid load fluctuations requires electromagnetic transient (EMT) models that capture fast converter and control dynamics. This paper develops a modular multi-fidelity EMT model of data center loads in PSCAD. The modular design supports flexible assembly of subsystem models for different power supply configurations. The multi-fidelity design incorporates switching models, average-converter models, and reduced-order models to balance simulation accuracy and computational efficiency according to analysis needs. The model also provides a systematic controller tuning procedure and supports control mode switching. Comparative simulations demonstrate how this data center load model responds to both grid-side and load-side disturbances and assess the accuracy and computational efficiency of models with three fidelity levels. The model is publicly available on GitHub.
quick_skim.tldr: This paper presents an open-source, modular, multi-fidelity EMT model of data center loads in PSCAD—combining switching, average-converter, and reduced-order representations with systematic controller tuning—to balance simulation accuracy and computational efficiency for power system studies.

quick_skim.title: Causal Discovery Bench: Can LLMs Autonomously Conduct Effective Experiments?
quick_skim.authors_text: Zhuoyang Liu, Ning Peng, Ming Shen, Zijun Gao
quick_skim.abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents get actively adopted for autonomous research, they must not only reason over existing evidence, but also design informative experiments, allocate resources, analyze sequential observations, and decide when to stop and make conclusions. Yet these capabilities remain poorly measured. We introduce Causal-Discovery-Bench (https://github.com/mshen1019/causal-discovery-bench), a verifiable sandbox with configurable structural equation models and resource constraints to evaluate sequential experimental design and causal discovery without domain-semantic cues. Across 3,802 episodes with 13 models from 5 vendors, we analyze agent behavior along 40 metrics in seven families. Agents' performance exhibits a four-level difficulty hierarchy spanning single-experiment design, sequential exploration of causal relationships, resource-aware experimentation balancing cost and statistical power, and autonomous resolution of conflicting evidence. We identify a substantial performance gap between causal inference from correctly curated evidence and navigating causal discovery through autonomous experimentation: Analyzing agents' action trajectories attributes 94.5% of their mistakes to experimental design rather than to inference, which is further consolidated with ablation studies. Relaxing resource constraints alone does not reliably resolve failures in sequential discovery. In contrast, basic statistical tools substantially improve performance across multiple model families, while advanced tools provide little additional benefit when models lack prerequisite lower-level capabilities.
quick_skim.tldr: Causal-Discovery-Bench reveals that LLM agents’ autonomous causal discovery is limited primarily by experimental design rather than inference—accounting for 94.5% of mistakes—and that basic statistical tools help substantially while advanced tools yield little benefit without prerequisite lower-level capabilities.

quick_skim.title: Quantum Natural Muon: Spectral-Natural Optimization for Variational Quantum Circuits
quick_skim.authors_text: Duong The Do, Duong Tung Nguyen
quick_skim.abstract: Training parameterized quantum circuits requires optimization methods that account for two distinct structures: the information geometry of quantum states and the matrix or tensor structure induced by circuit parameterization. We introduce Quantum Natural Muon (QNM), a spectral natural-gradient framework that applies polar normalization to circuit-semantic parameter blocks after damped quantum Fisher preconditioning. This ordering is essential: quantum Fisher preconditioning and blockwise polar normalization do not commute in general, so QNM is not an order-free composition of quantum natural gradient (QNG) and Muon. We show that Frobenius-matched polar mixing preserves active singular subspaces while raising a spectral floor and improving active conditioning, and that the resulting direction remains a controlled perturbation of QNG. For its distance-aware realization (DA-QNM), we further establish alignment, descent, and nonconvex stationarity guarantees for the normalized update, together with perturbation bounds under gradient and QFIM estimation error. Experiments on variational quantum eigensolving, weighted QAOA-MaxCut, and supervised quantum classification isolate the roles of quantum geometry, circuit-semantic spectral structure, and radius control. The strongest gains arise when the spectral blocks match the circuit structure, supporting the central principle that quantum-state and structured spectral geometries provide complementary information for variational quantum optimization.
quick_skim.tldr: The paper introduces Quantum Natural Muon (QNM), an order-sensitive spectral natural-gradient optimizer for variational quantum circuits that combines damped quantum Fisher preconditioning with blockwise polar normalization, and shows theoretical guarantees and empirical gains—especially when spectral blocks match circuit structure—for its distance-aware variant.

quick_skim.title: UniLatent: Cross-Embodiment Transfer via Latent Observation Alignment
quick_skim.authors_text: Yufei Ding, Yi Du, Weiduo Yuan, Hao Jiang, Dylan Goetting, Lawrence Yunliang Chen, Daniel Seita, Yue Wang
quick_skim.abstract: Robot datasets are costly to collect and are usually tied to a specific embodiment, making it difficult to reuse demonstrations across robots with different geometry, appearance, and kinematics. We introduce UniLatent, a cross-embodiment transfer framework that reduces the embodiment-induced observation gap in a shared latent space. UniLatent renders paired source-target robot observations in simulation and aligns a source visual encoder to a frozen target encoder. A policy trained on encoded source demonstrations can then run directly on target observations, with no pixel-level image translation. Across three simulation tasks and two target robot arms, UniLatent reaches up to 93% zero-shot success, exceeding the strongest pixel-translation baseline by over 30 points on average. In real-world xArm-to-Franka transfer, fine-tuning with only 10 target demonstrations per task yields 27/30 successful rollouts. Code, videos and data are available at https://selina2023.github.io/unilatent/.
quick_skim.tldr: UniLatent enables cross-embodiment robot transfer by rendering paired source–target observations at matched end-effector poses in simulation and aligning a source visual encoder to a frozen target encoder in a shared latent space, allowing policies trained on source demonstrations to deploy directly on target robot observations without pixel-level image translation.

quick_skim.title: MAGE: Towards Generalizable Multi-timescale EEG Representations
quick_skim.authors_text: Tuan-Kiet Doan, Van-Chien Nguyen, Trung-Hieu Tran, Quang-Hung Pham, Ngoc-Son Vu, Huy Phan, Phi Le Nguyen, Duc-Han Le, Nikola Simidjievski, Van-Tam Nguyen
quick_skim.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) data plays an important role in understanding human brain activity, with various major applications. While current approaches, which largely build on EEG foundation models, have demonstrated strong performance across datasets and tasks, they typically rely on a fixed temporal scale. This design choice limits their ability to capture characteristics of neural dynamic behavior, often spanning across multiple timescales, which are naturally captured in EEG recordings. To address this limitation, we propose MAGE (\textbf{Multi-timescale Adaptive Generalization for EEG}), a foundation model that dynamically adapts to capture and integrate information across different timescales. Specifically, MAGE combines two key mechanisms: (i) a novel multi-timescale attention mechanism, capable of learning representations across multiple temporal scales and (ii) a trainable aggregation module, that dynamically identifies and adapts to the most informative timescale of the input signal. Experimental results across seven datasets demonstrate that MAGE consistently outperforms existing EEG foundation models while using substantially fewer parameters. Moreover, our results support the hypothesis that different downstream tasks benefit from distinct temporal scales. All source code will be released.
quick_skim.tldr: MAGE is a multi-timescale EEG foundation model that uses multi-timescale tokenization, attention, and a trainable aggregator to dynamically adapt and fuse representations across temporal scales, consistently outperforming existing EEG foundation models with fewer parameters.

quick_skim.title: Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
quick_skim.authors_text: Weizhong Huang, Jinchao Zhang, Xiawu Zheng
quick_skim.abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems solve complex tasks through collaboration, but their growing, simultaneously resident key-value (KV) caches create a memory bottleneck. Applying single-model quantization policies independently ignores differences in agents' precision needs, potentially degrading collective reasoning. We introduce Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization (CoMixKV), which combines online sensitivity estimation with joint agent-layer bit-width allocation under a shared memory budget. To our knowledge, CoMixKV is the first mixed-precision KV-cache quantization framework to jointly allocate precision across simultaneously resident agent caches under such a budget. The estimator derives sensitivity from a local attention-error bound using recent queries, keys, and values, without calibration data, trial quantization, or additional model passes. A shared controller combines these scores with remaining quantizable capacity and byte-level storage costs to minimize total estimated error. Allocations are refreshed as agents start or finish and new observations become available. Selected widths apply only to newly quantized blocks; recent states retain native precision and previously quantized blocks remain unchanged. Across four benchmarks and three LLM backbones at average 2-bit, 3-bit, and 4-bit settings, CoMixKV achieves strong accuracy against the evaluated quantization baselines. At the average 3-bit setting on Gemma-4-31B-it, it achieves 68.35% average accuracy, exceeding the strongest quantized baseline by 0.59%. On Qwen3-32B, it reduces peak KV-cache memory by 32.08% and achieves a 1.38x inference speedup over FullKV.
quick_skim.tldr: CoMixKV is a coordinated mixed-precision KV-cache quantization framework that uses online attention-error sensitivity estimates to jointly allocate bit-widths across simultaneously resident LLM agents under a shared memory budget, improving accuracy while reducing memory and inference cost versus independent quantization baselines.

quick_skim.title: fNIRSAtlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Classification
quick_skim.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is a promising modality for brain-computer interfaces and cognitive state decoding, but progress in machine learning for fNIRS has been limited by small, isolated datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols. We introduce fNIRSAtlas, the largest open benchmark for fNIRS classification to date, comprising 23 classification tasks from 19 public data collections, spanning diverse experimental paradigms, including motor execution, motor imagery, mental arithmetic, working memory, and emotion recognition. fNIRSAtlas provides a fully automated pipeline from raw data to evaluation and defines standardized benchmark tasks for both cross-subject and within-subject classification, ensuring reproducible comparison of methods. We evaluate a variety of baseline models from fNIRS and related neuroimaging and time-series machine learning literature on the benchmark. Our results demonstrate that performance varies substantially across tasks and that methods validated on limited data -- especially deep learning approaches -- often fail to generalize beyond their original evaluation. fNIRSAtlas serves as an extensible, open, and reproducible benchmark to support more robust and cumulative progress in machine learning for fNIRS data. Our code and data can be found at https://fnirsatlas.github.io.
quick_skim.tldr: fNIRSAtlas is the largest open fNIRS classification benchmark, unifying 23 tasks from 19 public datasets into a standardized, automated pipeline for reproducible within- and cross-subject evaluation, and it shows that many models—especially deep learning methods—often fail to generalize beyond their original datasets.

quick_skim.title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems
quick_skim.authors_text: Hui Wang, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour, Jacob Chakareski, Ming Shi
quick_skim.abstract: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for real-time decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead. Because decision-relevant model differences need not grow with elapsed time, we define Age of Intelligence (AoInt) as a model-version-relative, client-specific, and action utility distortion, and formulate synchronization as a tradeoff between stale-decision regret and refresh cost. Furthermore, we develop Kullback-Leibler-aware AoInt Synchronization (KL-AoIntSync), which accumulates output-distribution changes using client-specific unlabeled probes, whereas Parameter-aware AoInt Synchronization (Param-AoIntSync) uses a server-broadcast scalar parameter change. Then, we establish pathwise guarantees with fixed client distributions, action sets, and utilities. The numerical results show that calibrated Param-AoIntSync reduces joint synchronization cost by 6.15% relative to an Instant-Parameters policy while performing comparably to KL-AoIntSync.
quick_skim.tldr: The paper introduces **Age of Intelligence (AoInt)**—a decision-utility-based, client-specific model staleness metric—and develops **KL-AoIntSync** and lightweight **Param-AoIntSync** policies to balance stale-decision regret against refresh cost in dynamic IoT model synchronization, with guarantees and a calibrated Param-AoIntSync achieving a **6.15% joint-cost reduction** over an Instant-Parameters baseline while matching KL-AoIntSync performance.

quick_skim.title: Transferring local rib responses to new component geometries in sheet forming with a graph-based Transformer
quick_skim.authors_text: Yingxue Zhao, Haoran Li, Haosu Zhou, Tobias Pfaff, Nan Li
quick_skim.abstract: Sheet metal components often consist of a global geometry, such as the corner radii and forming depth of a corner component, and local features added to it. During forming, both affect material flow. A surrogate learning all their combinations may need large training data. However, the same local feature type is often used on many global geometries. This study therefore partly decouples local features from the global geometry. The local-feature effect is first learned on one global geometry, needing fewer simulations than learning all combinations, then transferred to other global geometries via transfer learning, which can need fewer target simulations than training from scratch. A baseline-conditioned residual surrogate, R-BiLoGo, is proposed for ribs on the side walls of hot-stamped corner components. Its inputs are the baseline response and the geometric perturbation introduced by the ribs. Its outputs are the changes in displacement and thinning from the baseline. R-BiLoGo gave lower errors than a hierarchical graph-based model and a Transolver-based model on the source geometry, and on two of three selected target geometries after transfer. Across the 22 target geometries, transfer learning with 20 target simulations gave errors similar to or lower than training from scratch with 80 target simulations for about half of the targets. With the same 80 target simulations, transfer learning reduced errors for 95% of targets. The effect of the global geometry on transfer was studied with four parameter-free geometric descriptors and controlled variations across 4 corner subclasses. The benefit of transfer decreased with increasing surface distance and high-curvature change between source and target, and for targets shallower than the source. These trends were also seen in other corner types with a different magnitude.
quick_skim.tldr: The paper proposes R-BiLoGo, a baseline-conditioned residual graph Transformer that learns local rib effects on one hot-stamped corner geometry and transfers them to new global geometries with far fewer target simulations, while identifying geometric differences that reduce transfer benefit.

quick_skim.title: Topological Deep Learning Challenge 2026: Bridging the Gap
quick_skim.authors_text: Guillermo Bernárdez, Lev Telyatnikov, Mathilde Papillon, Marco Montagna, Louisa Cornelis, Louis Van Langendonck, Antonio Purificato, Bruno Neri, David Leko, Donatella Genovese, Eleonora Grassucci, Jan-Willem Van Looy, Johan Mathe, Lucia Testa, Luka Benić, Melanie Weber, Olga Zaghen, Pavlo Vasylenko, Raffael Theiler, Scott Mahan, Gaurav Khanal, Valentina Sánchez, Dario Loi, Gabriele Onorato, Prasanna Devadiga, Taejin Paik, Anier Velasco Sotomayor, Jonas Müller, Aarav Gupta, Riyan Patel, Grold Otieno Mboya, Pushparaj Devadiga, Adam Gohain, Dominik Filipiak, Michael Banf, Alireza Mohammadian, Amirreza Akbari, Gabriel Chaviano Díaz, Marcos Chávez Mesa, Ankit Grover, Rémi Bourgerie, Alessio Comparini, Ankit Kumar, Mohammad Yusuf, Devesh Kaushal, Francesco Orsi, Ghazal Mostofi, Kolya Lettl, Salwa Khattami, Gabriel Franco, Yelizaveta Falkouskaya, Jorge Luiz Franco, Kajal Singla, Fernando David Espinosa Iñiguez, Raj Patil, Eric Dolores-Cuenca, Luigi Petti, Chenguang Xu, Stefano Blando, Christine Zeh, Lennart Bastian, Kaden Zheng, Vihan Tiwari, Sud Athreya, Hisataka Kajita, Hugo Micheron, Rémi Devaux, Antoine Jardin, Tegan Emerson, Olga Fink, Nina Miolane
quick_skim.abstract: This paper describes the 2026 edition of the Topological Deep Learning Challenge: Bridging the Gap, hosted at the second Topology, Algebra, and Geometry in Data Science (TAG-DS) Conference. Where previous editions grew the modelling and data ecosystem of Topological Deep Learning (TDL), this edition set out to place Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Topological Neural Networks (TNNs) side by side under a single evaluation pipeline. Participants implemented recent state-of-the-art architectures in TopoBench, with Track 1 covering GNNs and Track 2 covering TNNs. They evaluated these implementations on shared synthetic benchmarks generated with GraphUniverse, which independently controls homophily, average degree and degree-distribution heaviness. The challenge yielded 68 qualifying submissions from 34 teams, spanning the graph, simplicial, cellular, hypergraph and combinatorial domains. For the first time, submissions were also tracked on a public leaderboard, which we summarize and analyze here. Our analysis finds that the differences between the submitted tracks are strongly task-dependent: the mean accuracy gap is modest on community detection, while on triangle counting the Track 1 mean error is 1.85 times the Track 2 mean. Several structurally informed GNNs also outperform the Track 2 mean on triangle counting.
quick_skim.tldr: TLDR: The 2026 Topological Deep Learning Challenge benchmarked GNNs and TNNs side by side in a shared TopoBench/GraphUniverse pipeline across 68 submissions, finding that their performance differences are strongly task-dependent—TNNs notably outperform GNNs on triangle counting, while the gap is modest on community detection.

quick_skim.title: Fast Accurate Quantum Monte Carlo without Metropolis Adjustment
quick_skim.authors_text: Reuben Cohn-Gordon, Gabriel Pescia, Sumner N. Hearth, Jakob Robnik, Uroš Seljak, Peter Lunts
quick_skim.abstract: In quantum systems, physical quantities of interest can be expressed as expectation values of a probability distribution, which allows their estimation by Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. This approach, an instance of Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC), plays a central role in obtaining predictions of system properties relevant to condensed matter and high energy physics. The use of Hamiltonian dynamics to design a Markov kernel, known as Hybrid or Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), is widespread in quantum applications. In this context, it is standard to use an HMC kernel that is ``adjusted'' with the Metropolis-Hastings (MH) criterion, so that estimates of expectations converge to their true value in the limit of infinite sample size. However, recent work in computational statistics suggests that an \emph{unadjusted} HMC kernel can be significantly more efficient, while safely maintaining an asymptotic bias which is small relative to the error arising from the variance of the finite sample size. We adapt this approach to the QMC setting, focusing on a challenging and high-dimensional \emph{spin-fermion} model of a quantum phase transition. We find that unadjusted methods outperform adjusted HMC in terms of effective sample size per gradient call, while retaining accurate results.
quick_skim.tldr: Using unadjusted Hamiltonian Monte Carlo without the Metropolis–Hastings correction on a high-dimensional spin-fermion quantum Monte Carlo model yields order-of-magnitude higher sampling efficiency than adjusted HMC while maintaining accurate results with controlled asymptotic bias.

quick_skim.title: Learning Across Heterogeneous Feature Spaces with Group Robustness
quick_skim.authors_text: Xenia Konti, Arjun Tschand, Chuan Hong, Nicoleta J. Economou-Zavlanos, Michael M. Zavlanos
quick_skim.abstract: In clinical applications, patients undergo different combinations of tests, and machine learning models must therefore ensure accurate predictions across heterogeneous feature spaces. Current approaches upweight the patients with the highest loss, without accounting for the limited predictive information in their features preventing their loss from going any lower. Moreover, when patients' feature spaces are fully disjoint, current methods reduce to training independent models, preventing knowledge transfer across them. We propose a framework for group robust learning across heterogeneous feature spaces, where groups are patients sharing a feature space. Since a high loss may simply reflect uninformative features, we instead optimize for worst-group excess loss, the gap between a group's loss and an estimate of its achievable optimum. To allow collaboration between groups, we use group-specific encoders mapping into a shared latent space in which learnable Gaussian anchors cluster patients by outcome. On tabular and imaging medical datasets, including fully disjoint feature settings, our framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods when groups differ in their optimal losses or cannot train a good model on their own, reducing worst-group loss by up to 79% and excess loss by up to 95% with up to 18$\times$ fewer parameters.
quick_skim.tldr: The paper proposes a group-robust learning framework for heterogeneous feature spaces that uses group-specific encoders mapped to a shared Gaussian-anchored latent space and optimizes worst-group excess loss, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on medical datasets.

quick_skim.title: Process then Retrieve: Investigating the Origins of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models
quick_skim.authors_text: Arpita Shanbhag, Julia Tran, Dhruv Mandala, Ayda Sultan
quick_skim.abstract: Understanding the origins of the modality gap in vision language models remains a significant challenge. This work investigates whether differences in information density between modality specific tokens at the embedding layer contribute to this imbalance. We show that text tokens enter the model with much lower semantic density than visual tokens, driving early layers to focus on processing text representations before combining them with vision. Through mechanistic analysis, we demonstrate that replacing vision token positions with their semantically closest text token counterparts elicits increased attention to those positions in early layers. These findings provide a foundation for addressing the modality gap and provide insight to improve multimodal reasoning in VLM architectures.
quick_skim.tldr: The paper shows that the vision-language modality gap arises because visually pre-encoded, semantically dense vision tokens enter the model before lower-density text tokens, causing early layers to process text first and integrate vision later—an asymmetry confirmed by replacing vision tokens with semantically similar text embeddings, which increases early cross-modal attention.

quick_skim.title: TrialJev: Open-Weight Single Pass Eligibility Scoring for Patient Trial Screening
quick_skim.authors_text: Omar Ibrahim, Grant Hamblin, Benjamin Haibe-Kains
quick_skim.abstract: Clinical trial screening requires assessing large numbers of patient-trial pairs to prioritize candidates for detailed eligibility review, often under restrictions on sharing patient records. We introduce TrialJev, an open-weight eligibility scorer that uses LoRA-adapted Qwen models and a pointer head to score natural-language answer options in a single forward pass, without autoregressive decoding. Trained on TREC Clinical Trials 2021 and evaluated on 6,975 eligible-or-excluded pairs from 50 unseen TREC 2022 synthetic patients, TrialJev achieves 80.97% (Qwen3.5-27B) and 81.84% (Qwen3.8-27B) accuracy, compared with 79.87% and 79.93% for LLMs fine-tuned on the same data to generate verdicts. In matched batch-1 measurements, verdict generation takes 2.45-2.70 times as long as the one-pass inference of TrialJev at 9B-27B. Under a common development-fitted decision correction, the two 27B TrialJev models reach 80.99% and 81.88% accuracy, compared with 81.28% for the proprietary hosted Jev API; paired confidence intervals include zero. TrialJev runs locally on a single GPU, requiring approximately 178 ms per pair at 27B, without transmitting patient text to an external model API. An A/B-logit ablation shows that avoiding decoding, rather than the pointer head alone, accounts for the measured efficiency advantage. TrialJev is intended for first-pass prioritization of candidate trials, complementing rather than replacing explanatory models and clinical review. Evaluation is limited to synthetic patients and implementation-specific timing, and clinical use has not been validated. Adapters, pointer heads, and model cards are released on Hugging Face.
quick_skim.tldr: TrialJev is an open-weight, single-pass patient–trial eligibility scorer built with LoRA-adapted Qwen models and a pointer head that achieves accuracy comparable to fine-tuned generative LLMs while running locally and 2.45–2.70× faster for first-pass screening prioritization.
